14.33.26.en: Yes, come, Lord Jesus, heavenly Bridegroom, and draw me into the procession of Your wedding; indeed, take my soul in Your embrace as a bride and a beautiful queen, upon whom the splendor of Your glory is reflected.

14.33.27.en: And may the heavenly beings glorify You for Your surpassing love for her!

14.33.28.en: v My soul praises You, because the time of her wedding has drawn near.

14.33.29.en: These are moments; sanctify them, and grant her to work by Your grace without ceasing.

14.33.30.en: Do not allow fornication to play with me, but sanctify every breath of my life.

14.33.31.en: v Let Your wisdom work in us, and protect us from the trials of the world.

14.33.32.en: And bring us into the pledge of the wedding banquet, that we may eat and drink and rejoice with the heavenly ones, and touch the glory You prepare for us. Glory to You, O All-loving toward mankind!

14.33.33.en: v Who can know the divine wisdom.

14.33.34.en: And by what name shall I call her, for You, O Wisdom of God, became incarnate for me.

14.33.35.en: The soul sees her, the heavenly bride, and is united with her in an eternal wedding that will never grow old or ancient!

14.33.36.en: I see her as a marvelous bird that carries me, and flies with me from glory to glory until I settle in heaven!

14.33.37.en: I see her as a beautiful queen whose voice is sweet; my soul looks at her as through the windows of the divine promises.

14.33.38.en: And I listen to her voice at the doors, as they open for me to cross over into the true royal glory.

14.33.39.en: I see her as a unique tree under which I take shade from the heat of trials.

14.33.40.en: I see her as a unique dwelling in which I dwell, and she dwells in me!

15.0.s.en: 1. Wisdom, mother and bride of him who fears the Lord

15.0.0.en: 1 He who fears the Lord will do this, and he who holds fast to the Law will obtain wisdom. 2 She will meet him as a mother, and receive him as a wife of virginity. 3 She will feed him with the bread of understanding, and give him the water of wisdom to drink; he will be established in her and not be moved, 4 and will rely upon her and not be put to shame, and she will exalt his standing among his companions, 5 and will open his mouth in the congregation, and fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothe him with a robe of glory. 6 He will inherit gladness and a crown of rejoicing and an everlasting name. 7 Foolish men will not attain her, but the sensible will meet her, and sinners will not see her, for she is far from pride and deceit. 8 Liars will not remember her, but the truthful will be found in her and will prosper, until they behold God.

15.0.1.en: He who fears the Lord will do this (take refuge in wisdom), and he who holds fast to the Law will obtain wisdom [1].

15.0.2.en: The previous chapter closed with the blessing of the one who practices wisdom, because she embraces him and protects him from the piercing heat of trials, and grants him the right to dwell in her glory (14:26-27). Now he declares her tenderness. She adopts the one who fears the Lord and becomes a mother to him, granting him of the fullness of her glory. As for him, he holds fast, keeping the Law and acquiring the gifts of wisdom.

15.1.0.en: She will come and meet him as a mother, and receive him as the wife of his youth [2].

15.1.1.en: Since the way of wisdom is a journey with its toils, Ben Sirach presents wisdom as a mother who embraces the one who seeks her and supports him in the midst of his striving, not allowing him troubles beyond his strength. She helps him on the way so that his soul is formed as an icon of the heavenly Bridegroom. She is a mother full of tenderness, able to form his depths so that he is made fit for the heavenly wedding.

15.1.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the saying: "A time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing" (Eccl 3:5) applies to married life in regard to bodily embrace: at the time of prayer, with the love of the spouses and their union together, they do not embrace during prayer; but as for wisdom as a spiritual wife, it befits the believer never to be separated from her embrace.

15.1.3.en: v When this wife is with a person, she gives birth to insight and thoughts and wise works. This is counted as a time to embrace... A person can embrace wisdom continually. This time is eternal [1].

15.1.4.en: St. Didymus the Blind In a letter that St. Ambrose sent to St. Irenaeus about the year 386 A.D., he commends him concerning the wise decision he took in answering the question whether there is a difference between those who received the faith from their childhood or early youth and those who received it after reaching manhood or late maturity. The letter came to reveal the difference between the God-fearing pious man who kept the Law from his youth and then came to know the Christian faith in the fear of the Lord, and the one who practiced sins in unbelief because of his idol worship, and in a late age believed in the Lord Christ. The first received divine wisdom through the Law, so wisdom embraced him from his childhood and kept him from the burden of evil pagan habits, and offered him spiritual food and sincere care like a mother tending her child or like a young wife who satisfied him with a pure relationship, so that he is not attached to any other and is not defiled by an impure relationship. Wisdom feeds him the bread of understanding, so that he does not hunger for adulterated food, and gives him spiritual waters to drink. From his childhood or early youth he labors in the Law or wisdom, and walks in the way of blameless truth. All look at him with a spirit of esteem and in the midst of the congregation all listen to his words with honor. His life is filled with gladness, and he enjoys a name of esteem that time does not erase.

15.1.5.en: St. Ambrose sees in the one who cleaves to the Lord Christ, the Word of God and incarnate Wisdom of God, as a Bridegroom, that his soul rejoices from his childhood or boyhood or youth at the presence of the Bridegroom working in the soul, granting her all her needs and sanctifying her. It is as though the saint invites us to cleave to the Lord without delay, so that we find in His divine care the spirit of fatherhood or motherhood, and enjoy the unity that is between bride and bridegroom in their youth.

15.1.6.en: v This soul that formerly received the experience of joy and gladness, when she acquired the first-born Word, did not fast, because her days were a feast and a banquet. The Bridegroom was present, offering her generously from all His abundant wealth, from the storehouses of heavenly food, and overflowing with the (spiritual) wine that makes glad the heart of man (Ps 104:15). Indeed, when she loses the Bridegroom by her deeds, she is asked to offer remorse in sackcloth for her sins, and to weep over herself, because Christ the virgin Word died and was crucified for her.

15.1.7.en: Sometimes the soul is married at an early age, so she suffers no other yoke, but from the beginning is bound to offer the flower of virginity through her faith in Christ, and is united with Him from the beginning in the mysteries of godliness, and receives training in holiness, like a young heifer bearing a (light) yoke.

15.1.8.en: So the soul of the person of Jewish origin (who fears the Lord), who is of the seed of the ancient patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob), if his soul keeps the course of a mother without stumbling, is counted worthy of a great merit, as a virgin bride of the Word (the Logos), and is like a mother who held fast to righteousness and went forth to meet Him, and He receives her as a bride who marries a virgin (cf. Sir 15:2) [2].

15.2.0.en: St. Ambrose She will feed him with the bread of understanding, and give him the water of wisdom to drink [3].

15.2.1.en: Our acquiring of wisdom is realized by our union with the Lord Christ, the Wisdom of God, the bread that came down from heaven. Wisdom as a mother offers the believer heavenly food, which is the bread of understanding, and spiritual drink, so that he does not suffer hunger or thirst, but always feels satisfied and refreshed.

15.2.2.en: v It is Christ who reveals the hidden and concealed mystery (Mt 11:25-27) and plants understanding in our hearts, because in Him and by Him are "all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Col 2:3), and by Him and with Him be glory and power from the Father with the Holy Spirit from generation to generation and to the ages of ages, Amen [3].

15.3.0.en: St. Cyril of Alexandria v Does any of you say that the philosophy discovered by the Greeks came as a result of human understanding? Yet I find the Holy Scripture saying that understanding is from God Himself. The psalmist counts understanding the greatest free gift, and exhorts the faithful, for David, in spite of the abundance of his trials and his knowledge, writes: "Teach me kindness and wisdom and knowledge, for I have believed thy commandments" [4].

15.3.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria He leans on her and does not fall, and holds fast to her and is not put to shame [4].

15.3.2.en: Since the seeker of wisdom fears falling on the way, wisdom cleaves to him as a helper so that he does not fall, and he relies upon her, so that his hope is not disappointed that he will truly become wise.

15.4.0.en: She exalts his standing side by side with his relatives, and opens his mouth in the midst of the congregation [5].

15.4.1.en: The work of wisdom does not stop, on the way of the believer's striving, at welcoming him [2], but she feeds him and satisfies him and gives him drink [3], and accompanies him that he may lean on her and draw his strength from her [4], and she also raises him before the congregation, as though honoring him here on earth with the pledge of the glory that he will enjoy in eternity as a bride and queen sitting at the right hand of the King of kings.

15.5.0.en: He will find gladness and a crown of rejoicing, and will inherit an everlasting name [6].

15.6.0.en: Foolish men do not find her, and sinners do not see her [7].

15.6.1.en: Ben Sirach reveals three groups that deprive themselves of wisdom by themselves, namely:

15.6.2.en: a. The group of fools [7]. b. The group of the proud [8]. c. The group of liars [8].

15.7.0.en: She is far from the proud, and liars will not keep her in their mind [8].

15.7.1.en: v He fulfills what the prophets rightly prophesied: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent." For He does not destroy His gift in them nor remove it from them, but what they attribute to themselves and what they did not receive from Him... this is despised as a weak and foolish thing found in the wise and strong of themselves. But this is the grace that heals the weak who do not swell up in pride with a blessedness of their own making, but rather in humility know their true misery [5].

15.7.2.en: v Let them think of Him who, when He came down to heal by the example of His humility the great mystery of the soul of man, pride! "God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, and the foolish things of the world to confound the wise - not truly wise but seeming so - and hath chosen the base things of the world, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are" [6].

15.7.3.en: St. Augustine v "Not many mighty, not many noble," for these also are filled with pride. Nothing causes failure with regard to the exact knowledge of God like haughtiness and attachment to wealth, for this draws a person to admire present things and to be indifferent to future things, and corrupts the ears with many entanglements. But God chose the foolish of the world, and this is a great sign of victory, since God overcomes by the unlearned [7].

15.7.4.en: v He called not only the unlearned but also the needy, the despised and the unknown, that He might put to shame those who are in high positions [8].

15.8.0.en: v God made everything with this aim: to shatter vainglory and pride and to humble haughtiness. He says: "Do you also busy yourselves with this work?" He did everything so that we should not make anything for ourselves for our own account, but ascribe everything to God. Do you give yourselves to this person or that? What forgiveness do you obtain? [9]

15.9.s.en: 2. Praise is a gift to him who fears the Lord

15.9.0.en: 9 Praise is not becoming in the mouth of a sinner, 10 for the Lord has not sent it to him. For praise is uttered by one who has wisdom, and the Lord makes him prosper.

15.9.1.en: Praise is not becoming in the mouth of a sinner, because the Lord has not sent it to him [9].

15.9.2.en: It befits all creation to praise the Creator, each in its own language: irrational creation bears witness to Him and praises Him for His power, His creativity and His care for it; the heavenly creation praises Him by its presence in heaven and its enjoyment of beholding His glory; as for mankind, it had the opportunity to cleave to God and so join the ranks of the heavenly ones, or to listen to the voice of the proud enemy and lose its fellowship with God. Sadly our first parents chose to withdraw from God their Creator, so sin and folly (ignorance) clung to them.

15.9.3.en: Man went out of Paradise hungry; the whole world cannot satisfy his heart or his senses or his mind, so he remained wandering on the face of the earth in great hunger until the holy God fills him with His satisfying Holy Spirit! In his hunger he cannot praise God, and at the same time he cannot enter into fellowship with God without praise. So we should not wonder if we are called to praise with purity of heart, and called to enjoy purity through praise. How is this realized?

15.9.4.en: By the incarnation of the Wisdom of God, that we may acquire Him and live by Him, we enjoy the wisdom from above. And wisdom gives us a satisfaction that generates praise in us, so that a person becomes like a nursing infant who rejoices in his mother, and all his feelings are stirred and all the members of his body respond to his joy to bring forth a hymn of true love that the tongue cannot express. True praise is not merely words we chant or tunes we learn, but in its depths it is a state of true joy that shakes the whole being of the believer: bodily, spiritually and psychologically, so that the tongue breaks forth in praise, and the heart dances with delight in the Lord, and the whole soul vibrates with heavenly, angelic melodies.

15.9.5.en: This is the work of wisdom, as she satisfies the soul and gives it drink and binds up its wounds, and restores to it its glory in Him, and removes from it the shame of sin and iniquity, so that it consecrates all its energies and gifts for His account, declaring the indwelling of the Holy One in it as the mystery of its sanctification and satisfaction and spiritual praise!

15.9.6.en: v Pray in peace and purity, chant with understanding and delight, and so you will be like a young eagle soaring in the heights of heaven.

15.9.7.en: The chanting of the Psalms calms the passions and restrains the pulses of the body's sufferings, and prayer drives the mind to be wise and sound in its actions...

15.9.8.en: The chanting of the Psalms is an image of the variety of the divine wisdom...

15.10.0.en: If you have not received the gift of God or the chanting of the Psalms, ask with fervor and persistence and you will receive [10].

15.10.1.en: Fr. Evagrius v If you live an evil life and utter good things, you are not praising God.

15.10.2.en: Again, if you begin to live well and attribute it to your own merits, you are no longer praising God. I do not want you to be a thief who mocks the cross of our Lord, nor do I want you, being His temple, to set aside His merits that are in you and veil His wounds.

15.10.3.en: If you are evil and persist in this evil of yours, I do not say to you that your praise does not profit you, but that you do not praise Me; I do not count that as praise.

15.11.0.en: Also, if you seem humble and good, but you are puffed up with your righteousness, despising others by comparing them with yourself, or exalt yourself boastfully because of your merits, you do not praise Me. Did not that Pharisee boast of himself thus when he said: "I thank thee, that I am not as other men are" (Lk 18:11) [11].

15.11.1.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles v Human beings were created to give much praise, and may they remember praise every day all the more!

15.11.2.en: The shining sun is not shining for itself nor does it travel for itself, but it has light to give light to men.

15.11.3.en: And for them the luminaries were set in the firmament (that is, the heaven), and for them the days and nights are of use.

15.11.4.en: For men there are discernment and knowledge and speech and voice, that they may give praise to the Most High in its place.

15.11.5.en: The mouth of man is perfected as though for the praise of the Lord, and he who has ceased to praise has become ungrateful.

15.11.6.en: And therefore you have a mouth, to praise with it and give thanks with it and rejoice with it and bless with it.

15.11.7.en: Praise, for you have the word that praises, and rejoice, for you have the voice full of melodies.

15.11.8.en: Give thanks, for you have mind and discernment, and bless, for you have become a vessel that speaks and is not silent.

15.11.9.en: You were nothing, and mercies made you something great, and since you have come to be, give thanks with wonder; why are you silent?

15.12.0.en: Enter into yourself and look at your person within you, for in you are found all the wonders of the creative power [12].

15.12.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh For praise is expressed by wisdom, and the Lord makes it flourish [10].

15.12.2.en: Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner; on the other hand the faithful believers are prepared for the new heavenly song (Rev 5:9), each believer enjoying it according to the purity of his heart. Therefore the Lord said: "In my Father's house are many mansions" (Jn 14:2).

15.12.3.en: v Although the wicked insist on keeping the feast and praising God as those at a feast, and burst into the church of the saints, God refutes them. He says to the sinner: "What hast thou to do to declare my statutes?" (Ps 50:16). And the gentle Holy Spirit rebukes them, saying: "Praise is not becoming in the mouth of a sinner" [9]. Sin has no fellowship at all with the praise of God. For the mouth of the sinner utters corrupt things, "the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things" (Prov 15:28).

15.13.0.en: How can we praise God with a defiled mouth, since opposite things cannot exist together. "For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?" (2 Cor 6:14). Paul, the minister of the Gospel, makes this clear. This is the condition of sinners and all who shun the Catholic Church, and the heretics and the schismatics, since they go out from glorifying God with the saints, they cannot continue as keepers of the feast in a fitting manner [13].

15.13.1.en: Pope St. Athanasius the Apostolic v If your praise is moved by lust, you are singing the old song. Let the words of the new song ring in your mouth; but if you are a sinner, nothing of the beautiful song is on your lips. It is better to be renewed and disciplined than to continue singing the same old song.

15.14.0.en: In truth you become a new person, even if you keep silent, and your praise will not reach human ears. Let your heart raise the new inward song (Ps 96:1), and it will reach the ear of God who has renewed you. You love even if you are silent. Your very love is the voice of the song offered to God [14].

15.15.0.en: v For this reason, when he said "Praise the Lord, for the psalm is good" (Ps 147:1), he said "and to our God praise is pleasant." How is praise pleasant to the Lord? If He is praised by our good life. Hear that praise which is pleasing to Him. He says in another place: "Praise is not becoming in the mouth of a sinner" (cf. Sir 15:9)... Praise can please a man when he hears someone praising him with skillful, tender feelings and with a sweet voice. But praise pleases God, whose ears are open to the heart and not the mouth, to the life of him who praises and not to his tongue [15].

15.15.1.en: St. Augustine The unclean spirit recognized the Lord Christ as the Holy One of God who became incarnate in humility (Mk 1:24). And he realized that the humility of the Lord overcomes his pride, and counted that the time had come for his condemnation, so he cried out, saying: "Ah! What have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? Thou art come to destroy us. I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God." The Lord rejected his testimony, rebuking him, saying: "Hold thy peace, and come out of him" (Mk 1:25).

15.16.0.en: v Even the demons utter the name of God, and yet they are demons... He rebuked them and cast them out. For this I ask you to be purified from this error (uttering the name of God in vain) [16].

15.16.1.en: St. John Chrysostom v What did the Savior say to Satan? "Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him" (Mk 1:25). For the truth has no need of the testimony of falsehood to it. "I did not come to be made known by your testimony, but to drive you out from one of My creatures." Praise from a sinner is not fitting... Be silent, for your silence is praise to Me. I have no need of your voice to praise Me, but your torment is praise to Me. Your torment honors Me.

15.17.0.en: Am I glad of your praise? I am glad of your going out. Be silent and come out of this man (Mk 1:25). As if He said to him: Go out of My house. What are you doing here in My dwelling? I want to enter, so go out and leave this man, this rational being. Come out of this man and leave Me My dwelling prepared for Me [17].

15.18.s.en: 3. He who fears the Lord and freedom of will

15.18.0.en: 11 Do not say: "My departure from her is from the Lord," but refrain from doing what He hates. 12 Do not say: "He has led me astray," for He has no need of a sinful man. 13 Every abomination is hated by the Lord, and is not loved by those who fear Him. 14 He made man in the beginning, and left him in the hand of his own choice, 15 and added to that His commandments and orders. 16 If you will, you will keep the commandments and fulfill His good pleasure. 17 And He set before you fire and water; you will stretch out your hand to whichever you wish. 18 Life and death are before man; whatever pleases him will be given to him.

15.18.1.en: God gave us freedom of will, so we cannot excuse ourselves by saying that the Lord wanted us to practice some error or commit a certain crime. Through human freedom Adam chose his destiny. Without freedom of will we could not enjoy the eternal reward or fall under eternal punishment.

15.18.2.en: v Just as the sun harms weak eyes not because of its own proper nature, so also with those who do not heed the word of God. So it is said in the case of Pharaoh that (God) hardened his heart. So it is with those who are fully insistent on resisting the words of God.

15.18.3.en: This is the manner of Scripture, as it is said: "He gave them up to a reprobate mind" (Rom 1:28)... For the writer here does not present God as Himself doing these things, but shows that they happen through the wickedness of others. So in order to terrify the hearer, the writer says: "God hardened," "He gave them up."

15.19.0.en: And to show that He does not give us up nor leave us except if we ourselves wish it, hear what he says: "Do not your sins separate between me and you?" (Isa 59:2) LXX. And Hosea says: "You have forgotten the law of your God, and I also will forget you" (Hos 4:6) LXX. And He Himself says: "How often would I have gathered thy children together... and ye would not!" (Lk 13:34)... Knowing this, let us exert every effort not to leave God, but to hold fast to the care of our souls and love for one another. Let us not cut off our members, for this is the work of madmen, but the more we see them in an evil state, the more we show them compassion [18].

15.20.0.en: St. John Chrysostom v Paul counsels us to increase our speed. He says: Run, that ye may obtain. For he himself, in swift motion, wished to reach what was before him, forgetting what was behind. He was truly a swift-moving wrestler, observing with all exactness the resistance of his opponent. He is well armed, safe in every step he takes; he will not direct the weapon in his hand against an empty shadow, but attacks his enemy with the living blows that he aims at him [19].

15.21.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa v He did not rebuke those who left Him nor threaten them violently, but rather turned to His disciples, saying: "Will ye also go away?" (Jn 6:67), truly respecting the law by which man exercises his freedom and remains in his freedom of will to choose death or salvation [20].

15.21.1.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr Do not say: "The Lord made me fall, for He does not do what He hates [11].

15.21.2.en: God's sanctification of freedom of will appears in the life of Samson, who performed wonderful deeds that signify the saving work of Christ and His care for His people, and when he wished to go to a harlot He did not compel him to turn from it (Judg 16:1-3). When he walked in the Lord he bore the reflection of the splendor of his Lord, and when he fell by his own will he was in shame and humiliation.

15.21.3.en: v In the story of Samson there are beautiful deeds and defiled ones, some exalted and some base, and it befits us to tell the whole truth.

15.21.4.en: When he bore the mysteries of his Lord he was beautiful, and when he fell from his splendor he became defiled and hateful.

15.21.5.en: He was beautiful when he brought forth the sweet from the bitter, and became abased when he revealed his secret to a (harlot) woman...

15.21.6.en: The Lord is very gentle and longsuffering toward the sons of men, and when they fall it is not He who pushes them to it. The great things Samson did were from God, but the other evil ones were from Samson alone. The Lord did not command him to go to the woman, but he desired it himself, and the Lord did not prevent him, since he was free.

15.21.7.en: When he was thirsty and asked for water the Lord gave it to him and he drank, and when he wished to go to a harlot he went in because he wished...

15.21.8.en: Perhaps Samson's going to the harlot was by the permission of the dispensation, that his fall might be for your salvation.

15.22.0.en: And he will be a mirror for you that reveals your faults, so you see yourself, and do not fall as he fell [21].

15.22.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Do not say: "He led me astray," for He has no need of a sinful man [12].

15.22.2.en: The Lord hates every abomination, and they are not loved by those who fear Him [13].

15.23.0.en: v Man acquires goodness from God, for He is good. But evil is subject to him from within [22].

15.23.1.en: v God is good, but man is evil. There is no evil in heaven, nor true goodness on earth. But the sensible man chooses the better. He learns to know God the Almighty, and to thank Him and glorify Him, and to subdue his body even before death, and not to satisfy the feelings (lusts) of the body, because he knows their harm and their wicked work [23].

15.23.2.en: St. Anthony the Great He created man in the beginning, and left him to consult his (human) will [14].

15.23.3.en: St. Basil the Great does not lay the blame on the body or the soul, for the good God created them good, but man, since his will is corrupted, practices a holy life neither with his body nor with his soul. God created man able to practice righteousness, or to do evil. He also granted him freedom of choice (cf. Sir 15:14). Even after the fall into rebellion against God He did not remove from him the gift of freedom of choice (Sir 15:15), although man corrupted his free will, so that he became in need of God's grace to practice righteousness, without man being compelled to practice righteousness by force against his will.

15.23.4.en: v If the soul had no power to subdue the passions of the body and to tame its movements, they (the heretics) would have an argument in blaming the body. But the valiant strivers have conquered the sufferings of the body, and tamed its movements, and used it for benefits, and it is the soul that must be blamed, because it grew slack, though it has authority over the body.

15.23.5.en: And the soul also has no evil by its nature - God forbid - but evil was found in it because it did not do the good for which it was given the power and the choice. For evil in man is nothing but the absence of virtue, and where there is no virtue there truly is evil [24].

15.23.6.en: v First, we must affirm the truth that we have indeed received from God the power to carry out the commandments He has given us, so that our obligation to them may not be an odious thing, as though the commandments were foreign to us and unexpected, and demanded of us. We do not feel that they are unreal (imaginary), as though we were asked to offer what has not been given to us [25].

15.23.7.en: v This power given to us by God we use rightly and fittingly, and so we spend our whole life in the holiness of a virtuous life. But if we misuse it, we fall gradually prey to vice. Thus the definition of vice is the wrong use, and the violation of the Lord's commandment, of what was given to us by God for a good purpose. In the same way, the definition of the virtue that God requires of us is the use of these gifts with a good conscience according to the Lord's command.

15.23.8.en: This is the case, and we apply it to love. For we have received the commandment to love God, and we have the instinctive power to love from the first moment of our creation [26].

15.23.9.en: v This needs no external proof, for every person can discover it by himself within himself. By nature we desire what is beautiful, even if the conceptions of beauty differ widely from one person to another [27].

15.23.10.en: St. Basil the Great If you will, you will keep the commandments, and faithfully fulfill His good pleasure [15].

15.23.11.en: v Question: What are the signs within us that indicate love toward God?

15.23.12.en: Answer: The Lord taught us that when He said: "If ye love me, keep my commandments" (Jn 15:14) [28].

15.23.13.en: v If a person confesses the Lord and hears His words, but does not obey His commandments, he is condemned even if he has a divine privilege, having been granted the gift of spiritual gifts (Mt 7:21-23) [29].

15.23.14.en: v Question: Who is (he who is called) a bruised reed or smoking flax? And how is the first not broken, and the other not quenched (Mt 12:20)?

15.23.15.en: Answer: I reckon that the bruised reed is he who fulfills God's commandment under the influence of a certain passion. No one may break him or cut him off, but rather heal him, as the Lord did when He taught: "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them" (Mt 6:1). And the Apostle commands us: "Do all things without murmurings and disputings" (Phil 2:14). And in another place: "Nothing through strife or vainglory" (Phil 2:3).

15.23.16.en: And the smoking flax is he who fulfills the commandment without burning desire and complete zeal, but with sluggishness and without order, and we must not restrain such a one, but rather urge him by reminding him of God's judgments and promises [30].

15.23.17.en: St. Basil the Great He sets before you fire and water, and you stretch out your hand to what you wish [16].

15.23.18.en: In the creation of man "God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good" (Gen 1:31). This does not mean that He created man incapable of falling, but He created him in His image and likeness, and granted him the highest gift, which is freedom of will. He did not create in him anything evil, but granted him to choose his way with his full will, so that if he clung to his Creator and walked by the grace of God he would increase in splendor and glory. But since he isolated himself from his Creator he returned to his earthly origin and became corrupt. God did not create man evil, but man loved darkness more than light, and became in need not only of receiving forgiveness for the iniquities he had done, but also of someone to sanctify his will and works. He sets before you fire and water; man has the right to choose between falling into judgment (the eternal fire) or salvation by sonship to God through baptism.

15.23.19.en: Life and death are before men, and what a man chooses will be given to him [17].

15.23.20.en: God sanctifies freedom of will for men. For man has the right to choose between "fire and water," and "life and death." This echoes what is stated in the Book of Deuteronomy to urge the believer to choose (Deut 30:19).

15.23.21.en: God in His wonderful love for humanity desires that all men be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 2:4). At the same time He is careful to honor man, so He does not offer His heavenly gift without revealing man's freedom. He offers him His grace to support him. Perhaps by fire He means that the believer strives, bearing the fires of trials and troubles with joy for the sake of eternity, and does not stretch his hand to water, that is, the desire for a cold life and slackness. It is man's right to choose life through the grace of God, or in slackness to choose eternal death [17]. When the believer chooses eternal life and not death he cleaves to Christ, who reigns in his heart, and death is destroyed as the last enemy (1 Cor 15:26).

15.23.22.en: v "For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet" (1 Cor 15:25), so that "the last enemy that shall be destroyed is death" (1 Cor 15:26). When this is destroyed, life alone (Christ) remains, in whom we believe (Jn 11:25). As long as death stands among men, those whom it holds captive do not believe in life (in Christ) [31].

15.23.23.en: v Life is Christ (Jn 14:6), and death indicates the last enemy (1 Cor 15:26), that is, Satan. Therefore the soul takes its decision whether it chooses life, that is, Christ, or turns toward death, that is, Satan.

15.23.24.en: Origen v Pelagius quoted the following passage from the Psalm (Ps 109:17): "He loved cursing, and it came upon him; he delighted not in blessing, and it was far from him." But who does not know that this is an error, that it was not fulfilled through nature as God created it, but through the human will that drew away from God? The truth is that even if he did not love cursing and desired blessing, yet in this example he denies that his will was helped by divine grace, and by his ingratitude and impiety he was deprived of governing himself, so he was deprived of divine leadership, and destruction was brought upon him. This can be discovered by discipline, that he was unable to govern himself.

15.23.25.en: In the same way, in another passage that Pelagius quotes... He set before you fire and water, and you stretch out your hand to whatever you wish. Life and death are before men, and what they choose is given to them? (cf. Sir 15:16-17). It is clear that if he puts his hand into the fire, and if evil and death please him, his human will is responsible. And on the contrary if he loves goodness and life, he does not make his will alone determine the choice, but his will that is helped by the divine will. For the eye is not sufficient in itself to see, that is, in darkness, and to see it is not enough for it to have its own light, unless an external light helps it and makes it able to do so, otherwise the cries are in vain: "Let not the lust of gluttony nor fornication possess me" (cf. Sir 23:6).

15.23.26.en: God grants this privilege to those over whom He reigns, and not to those who think that they are able to govern themselves, and who in proud stubbornness exalt their own will and deny that God leads them [32].

15.23.27.en: St. Augustine Pelagius quoted these two passages among other passages of Holy Scripture to justify his insistence that everything in man's life is governed by his will, ignoring the grace of God.

15.23.28.en: v Everything we have already pointed out, that is, the good and the evil, is contained in the two passages. For heaven and hell, Christ and Satan, the height and the depth are proposed to us. By God's grace He made it possible for each one of us to choose and to stretch out his hands to what he wants.

15.23.29.en: Christ has authority over uprightness and the narrow way, but Satan proposes the wide-open, broad way. The first calls man to heaven, and the latter moves man toward hell. One raises man to the heights, and the other presses him down to the depths. Satan shows a false sweetness in order to draw man to true bitterness. Christ calls him to a few hardships in order to lead him to extended blessedness. If we open only our bodily eyes, the broad, wide-open way deceives us, but if we listen to the insight of our hearts, the narrow and hard way keeps us safe [33].

15.23.30.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles v Just as the body without the soul is dead, so the soul without the mind is idle (barren) and unable to inherit God [34].

15.23.31.en: v Just as heaven is invisible, so goodness is invisible. And just as what is on earth is visible, so evil too is visible. Goodness cannot be compared, and man with his mind may choose the better... [35]

15.24.s.en: 4. The eyes of the Lord are on those who fear the Lord

15.24.0.en: 19 For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things, 20 and His eyes are on those who fear Him, and He knows every work of man. 21 He has not commanded anyone to be hypocritical, nor permitted anyone to sin, 22 for He does not love a multitude of ungodly children who have no good in them.

15.24.1.en: Great is the wisdom of the Lord, and He is mighty in authority, and sees all things [18].

15.24.2.en: His eyes are on those who fear Him, and He Himself knows every work of man [19].

15.25.0.en: He has not commanded anyone to be wicked, nor permitted anyone to sin [20].

15.25.1.en: v We must take care lest anyone think that the crimes that those who commit what makes them not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Cor 6:10) do not utter, they commit daily and think they are delivered from them by almsgiving. Our life must change to what is better, and alms must be given to appease God for past sins, and they must not suppose that by them they purchase a license to commit the same sins, as those in an immunity that prevents them from judgment. "He has permitted no one to sin" (cf. Sir 15:20), even if by His mercy He washes the sins that we have already committed [36].

15.26.s.en: Nail Your fear into my heart, that my soul may rejoice in Your wisdom and Your commandment!

15.26.0.en: v What shall I ask of You, O All-loving?! Nail Your fear within me, that Your wisdom may be poured out in me, and I may enjoy Your wisdom and find Your commandments sweet and delight in them. Then my life will turn into an unceasing hymn of thanksgiving!

15.26.1.en: Your wisdom is my mother, she carries me in her embrace, and offers me the heavenly good things.

15.26.2.en: And she is the beautiful bride, ever rejoicing; I am united with her, and the joy of the Spirit overflows within me; with confidence and boldness I meet her, for she is not a stranger to me. By her I go forth toward heaven day by day.

15.26.3.en: I hunger for her, and she offers me the bread of understanding and the spirit of discernment. My hunger and thirst for her increase, and I enjoy new glories!

15.26.4.en: No shame or disgrace overtakes me, for by Your grace I put on the robe of Your righteousness, I who am dust and ashes!

15.26.5.en: v In Your company, O my Savior, my soul rejoices and the journey of my life turns into the road to the eternal wedding.

15.26.6.en: I need neither a scrip nor a staff (Mt 10:10; Lk 9:3).

15.26.7.en: Instead of a scrip my soul is satisfied with the heavenly food (Wis 19:20).

15.26.8.en: And instead of a staff she protects me from the powers of darkness.

15.26.9.en: I embrace her with my heart and mind without ceasing, eternally. So my life turns into a constant feast and a banquet that never empties.

15.26.10.en: I lean upon her and do not fall. And if I fall through my weakness, she stretches out her hand and raises me with hope, without despair.

15.26.11.en: v My soul is grieved over the foolish, the proud and the liars. Shine Your light upon them, that they may return to You.

15.26.12.en: Draw them to You and renew their life. Instead of corruption may they enjoy holiness.

15.26.13.en: And instead of bitterness may their mouth be opened in praise! And instead of haughtiness may they enjoy the sweetness of Your meekness.

15.26.14.en: You grant man the spirit of power, so that by You he defies evil, and the enemy of good with all his devices cannot rob him from You; by You the smoking flax turns into a flame of burning love. And darkness is dispelled where You rise, O Sun of righteousness.

15.26.15.en: v You set fire and water before every human being; we pass through the fire and it turns into dew, and we cross the Jordan, and receive sonship.

15.26.16.en: And by You and with You we cross the waters of the Jordan, and receive the spirit of sonship by baptism.

15.26.17.en: You are our eternal, immortal life; by You the sting of death is broken, and the doors of eternity are opened before us!

15.26.18.en: You lift us to the heights to be in Your embrace, and the devil is unable to bring us down to the netherworld!
